name: OpenCode
tagline: An open source AI coding agent that runs in your terminal and edits your repo directly.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The client itself is open source and free; costs come from model tokens, either your own provider keys or hosted credits.

verdictSummary: The core of a terminal coding agent is a loop: send the conversation to a model, let it call tools like read, write, edit, bash, grep, feed results back, repeat. An agent can write a working version of that in one sitting and you will be genuinely surprised how usable it is on small repos. What takes much longer is everything around the loop: a TUI that does not flicker, sane diff previews and approval gates, context compaction that does not lose the thread, session resume, multi-provider routing, LSP awareness, MCP servers, and the dozens of prompt tweaks that stop the model from confidently deleting things. Also worth saying out loud: OpenCode is already open source and free to run with your own keys, so the honest reason to build your own is curiosity or a very specific workflow, not cost. Weekend build, real gaps, and a free incumbent sitting right there.
coreLoopDIY: A CLI that streams a model's responses and lets it read, write, patch, search, and run shell commands in your working directory behind an approval prompt.
requirements: An API key for a tool-calling model (Anthropic or OpenAI)
Willingness to run model-authored shell commands on your own machine
Git, so you can revert when it goes wrong
whatYouLose: A polished TUI with diff review, scrollback, and keybindings that do not fight your terminal
Context compaction and session resume that actually survive long tasks
Multi-provider and local-model routing without rewriting your client
LSP and MCP integrations, plus the agent/subagent and permission machinery
Hundreds of other people finding the prompt and tool-safety bugs before you do
moatNotes: No data moat at all, the moat is prompt craft, tool ergonomics and the integration surface. Hard to copy fully, impossible to copy by accident.
whyPeopleStillPay: Mostly they do not pay for the client, they pay for tokens, and that is the honest shape of this market. What the project earns is attention: it is the thing that already works on day one, handles the model switching, keeps sessions coherent across hours of work, and has had its sharp edges filed down by real usage. A homegrown agent loop is a great weekend and a genuinely good way to understand what these tools do, but you will spend your next month maintaining a worse version of free software rather than shipping whatever you opened the editor for.
notes: Building your own coding agent is one of the best teaching exercises available right now, and one of the worst uses of a maintenance budget.
prompt:
Build a minimal terminal AI coding agent in a new Node 20 + TypeScript project. No framework menus: use tsx for running, Anthropic's SDK for the model, and nothing else that is not required.

Scope, in:
- A CLI entrypoint `agent` that takes a task string or drops into an interactive prompt loop in the current working directory.
- An agent loop: send messages plus tool definitions to claude-sonnet via the Messages API with streaming, execute any tool calls, append results, repeat until the model stops calling tools or a 40-step cap is hit.
- Tools: read_file, write_file, edit_file (exact string replace, fail loudly if the match is not unique), list_files (respect .gitignore), grep (ripgrep if present, else a JS fallback), run_bash.
- Safety: every write_file, edit_file and run_bash call prints a colored unified diff or the exact command and waits for y/n/a on stdin. `a` allows that tool for the rest of the session. Nothing outside the cwd, ever, reject absolute paths and ..
- Sessions: append every message and tool result as JSONL under .agent/sessions/. `agent --resume` reloads the most recent one.
- Token hygiene: truncate any tool result over 8000 characters with a clear marker, and when the transcript exceeds roughly 100k tokens, summarize the oldest half into a single system note.
- A system prompt that tells the model to read before editing, make small targeted edits, and run tests when they exist.

Scope, out: no TUI library, no web UI, no accounts, no telemetry, no MCP, no LSP, no multi-provider abstraction, no subagents.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY comes from .env via dotenv. Commit .env.example, gitignore .env and .agent.

Write a README with install, one usage example, and an explicit warning that this executes model-authored shell commands and should only be run inside a git repo with a clean working tree.
